standard.title: Character form and complex grammatical structures
standard.description: apply knowledge of character form and function, and complex grammatical structures and features, to predict meaning and to compose a wide range of texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can analyse character components, apply stroke conventions, and use a range of sentence structures including complex constructions (AC9LCH8EU02). They have inferred meaning from morphological knowledge. They have not yet analysed sequences of unfamiliar characters using component patterns to predict meaning, compared simplified and traditional forms systematically, or applied complex literary language and grammatical features in extended texts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply knowledge of character form and function and complex grammatical structures to predict meaning and compose a wide range of texts — including analysis of simplified/traditional forms, polysemy, literary language, and advanced grammatical features.

nodes.label: Advanced character analysis and prediction
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse sequences of unfamiliar characters using component patterns to predict meaning, compare simplified and traditional forms, and determine precise morpheme meanings from context.
nodes.minimum_width: Predict the meaning of at least three unfamiliar characters using component analysis, compare at least two simplified/traditional form pairs, and determine the precise meaning of at least two polysemous morphemes from context.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse sequences of unfamiliar characters to predict meanings; compare simplified and traditional character forms; analyse and compare unfamiliar characters in print and online texts; apply word formation understanding when comparing translations; discriminate correct forms and sounds of characters with multiple readings.
wider: Research the relationship between simplified and traditional forms for a set of characters — explain what was simplified, the historical rationale, and what (if anything) is lost or gained
Investigate a productive morpheme — identify all words it appears in, document the semantic pattern, and generate new combinations with verification
nodes.hinge_reason: Advanced character analysis and prediction are the prerequisites for independent reading of complex texts. Students who cannot predict meaning from component patterns cannot approach genuinely unfamiliar texts strategically — which is the threshold the Y9-10 descriptor marks.

response_modes.reason: Character prediction requires systematic application of a multi-layered framework — component identification, semantic pattern, phonetic contribution, contextual disambiguation. Explicit strategy instruction with graduated practice builds this systematic analytical capacity.

success_criteria: Predicts the meaning of at least three unfamiliar characters using component analysis
Determines the precise meaning of at least two polysemous morphemes from context

nodes.label: Complex grammatical features and literary language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply complex grammatical features — modal and auxiliary verbs, abstract nouns, literary particles — and identify how grammatical features differ between literary and everyday language.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a text demonstrating at least three complex grammatical features correctly, including at least one that differs between literary and everyday registers.
nodes.typical_width: Apply modal and auxiliary verbs across text types; use abstract nouns in procedural and creative texts; apply advanced punctuation; explore literary language and how grammatical features differ from everyday speech; apply tense knowledge in formal and informal text types; identify how sentence structures convey messages effectively.
wider: Analyse a target language literary text for grammatical features that distinguish it from everyday speech — explain each feature and discuss the literary effect it creates
Compare own extended writing with a literary model — identify specific grammatical features of the model not present in own writing and experiment with incorporating them

response_modes.reason: Complex grammatical features and literary language require repeated production across varied text types before they become reliable. Regular extended writing tasks across different registers — formal, informal, literary — build the flexible grammatical competence needed.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students may know literary language from home exposure to traditional texts or family literacy. Width investment here bridges this cultural knowledge — making implicit literary language awareness explicit and productive in formal writing.
success_criteria: Produces a text demonstrating at least three complex grammatical features correctly
Includes at least one feature that differs between literary and everyday registers

nodes.label: Composing a wide range of texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply full character and grammatical knowledge to compose a wide range of texts — formal, informal, procedural, literary, multimodal — across diverse contexts and purposes.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose at least two texts of different types applying full character and grammatical knowledge appropriately for each text type.
nodes.typical_width: Apply character and grammatical knowledge across a wide range of text types — reports, plans, diaries, scripts, literary works, multimodal productions; adapt grammatical choices for context, purpose and audience; respond to diverse stimuli with appropriate grammatical selection.
wider: Compose a text that deliberately uses a specific grammatical or literary feature for rhetorical effect — explain the choice and compare with an alternative approach
Review and annotate own extended writing for grammatical accuracy and register appropriateness — identify patterns and develop a targeted improvement plan

response_modes.reason: Wide-range text composition integrates character analysis (node 1) and complex grammatical features (node 2) into full productive literacy at the highest level of this pathway. The teaching investment is in creating genuinely varied, purposeful composition tasks across text types — not only narrative or only formal.

success_criteria: Composes at least two texts of different types applying full character and grammatical knowledge
Grammatical and vocabulary choices are appropriate to each text type and purpose
